stories.headline: MKBHD Announces Fresh Start with New Video “I’m Starting Over”
stories.summary: Tech YouTuber Marques Brownlee (MKBHD) posted a video titled “I’m Starting Over,” signaling a shift in his content strategy. He hints at revamping his channel’s approach, though details of the changes remain limited in the release.

stories.headline: Review: Kevin DeYoung’s ‘Church History for Everyone’ Makes the Past Accessible
stories.summary: The Gospel Coalition essay evaluates DeYoung’s latest work, arguing that a clear, narrative‑driven approach to church history can equip modern believers with essential context for today’s challenges.

stories.headline: MKBHD Teases Secret Project
stories.summary: Tech creator MKBHD has published a placeholder video hinting at a forthcoming announcement. The upload contains standard YouTube backend configuration data rather than actual content. Fans will have to wait for a follow-up release to discover the details of the secret project.

stories.headline: PVL All-Filipino Conference Heads to Decisive Semifinal and Finals
stories.summary: The Premier Volleyball League All-Filipino Conference is wrapping up its opening Siklab Series at the Philsports Arena in Pasig City. Creamline secured its spot in the championship after defeating Choco Mucho, while Farm Fresh and Nxled face off in a winner-take-all semifinal match to determine the final challenger. The best-of-three championship series is scheduled to begin on November 28.

stories.headline: A Brief History of Volleyball: From Mintonette to Olympic Sport
stories.summary: William G. Morgan invented volleyball in 1895 at a Massachusetts YMCA, originally naming the sport mintonette. It later expanded internationally through the FIVB, debuting at the Olympics in 1964 for indoor play and 1996 for beach volleyball. Today, the sport draws massive crowds, including a record 92,003 spectators at a 2023 match in Nebraska.

stories.headline: Marques Brownlee Follows Up on Editorial Trust and Integrity
stories.summary: Popular tech creator Marques Brownlee has published the second installment in a series examining whether audiences can trust his product assessments. The release addresses channel credibility and transparency standards across his gadget coverage and review processes.

stories.headline: MKBHD Deploys Holiday Tech Guide Highlighting Budget Gear Under $50
stories.summary: Popular tech creator MKBHD published his annual holiday gift guide featuring top-tier gadgets priced under $50. The curation targets affordable tech options suitable for holiday shoppers looking for quality electronics on a budget. The accompanying video details specific hardware picks.

stories.headline: Marques Brownlee Ranks His Favorite Halloween Candy
stories.summary: In a light‑hearted video, Marques Brownlee (Marques Blind) shares his personal ranking of Halloween treats, offering quick commentary on taste, texture, and nostalgic appeal.

stories.headline: Marques’ Studio Spotlights Obscure Foldable Phones
stories.summary: The Studio episode features Marques highlighting a selection of lesser‑known foldable smartphones, explaining their unique designs and why they’ve flown under the mainstream radar.

stories.headline: Neil Paine Launches 2026-27 NBA Elo Forecast and LAKER Ratings
stories.summary: Analyst Neil Paine has released his 2026-27 NBA season projections, utilizing a refined Elo model trained on historical game logs dating back to 1946-47. The updated system maintains separate tracks for short-term regular season form and durable playoff performance. These ratings drive ongoing game simulations, championship odds, and player evaluations on the LAKER leaderboard.

stories.headline: NBA Daily Roundup: Trade Rumors, Power Rankings, and Team Updates
stories.summary: Basketball Intelligence's November 26 edition covers Tom Thibodeau's potential return to the NBA and Karl-Anthony Towns' support for the move. The newsletter also highlights team-specific updates, including the Nets snapping a five-game losing streak against the Bucks and injury recovery news for Pacers star Tyrese Haliburton.

stories.headline: Basketball Intelligence Data Roundup
stories.summary: Recent NBA analytics highlight Victor Wembanyama dominating both offensive and defensive leaderboards simultaneously. Meanwhile, historical schedule analysis shows the 2022-23 Sacramento Kings benefited from unusually favorable injury luck against opponents.

stories.headline: Exploring Moral Clarity Through Confession and Ebenezer
stories.summary: The Gospel Coalition features theological essays emphasizing moral clarity, repentance, and the faithfulness of God in challenging times. Content covers historical perspectives, Christian benchmarks, and pastoral insights designed to guide believers. These resources address foundational doctrines and contemporary church issues alike.

stories.headline: Decoding the Volleyball Dig: Rules and Statistics
stories.summary: According to the NCAA Volleyball Statisticians' Manual, a dig is officially recorded when a player successfully passes an opponent's attack to keep the rally alive. Serves do not qualify as digs, and the statistic applies regardless of whether the defensive contact is made with forearms, hands, or a pancake move. The primary objective is ensuring play continues, differentiating a true defensive save from a routine serve receive.

stories.headline: Llama-cpp-rdna-boosts Fork Delivers Major Speed Gains for AMD Graphics Cards
stories.summary: As bespoke inference engines proliferate, a minimal fork called llama-cpp-rdna-boosts offers targeted optimizations for AMD hardware. The repository successfully increases token generation and prefill speeds without resorting to the aggressive model-manipulation shortcuts seen in other emerging engines.

stories.headline: Congo Ebola Outbreak Surpasses 12,000 Cases Amid Rescinded Responders
stories.summary: The deadliest and fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in Congo's history has crossed 12,000 confirmed cases with nearly a 50 percent fatality rate. Ongoing armed conflict between rebels and the army, combined with community mistrust, severely hampers containment efforts for the rare Bundibugyo virus.

stories.headline: Kim Jong Un Inspects Nuclear Facilities and Demands Arsenal Expansion
stories.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un visited weapons-grade nuclear material production facilities to order an expansion of the country's nuclear arsenal. The move follows his decision to ignore an overture from U.S. President Donald Trump during a recent Asian tour, signaling a firm rejection of future disarmament talks.

stories.headline: Demystifying Uncertainty in Machine Learning Models
stories.summary: Machine learning models inherently carry uncertainty, which stems from either incomplete data or unobservable factors. Distinguishing between epistemic uncertainty, which can be reduced with more data, and aleatoric uncertainty, which cannot, is vital for reliable decision-making. Grasping these probabilistic fundamentals helps developers choose realistic model assumptions despite underlying inaccuracies.

stories.headline: Zelensky Slams US Focus on Middle East and Trump-Putin Friendship
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky criticized the US for inadequate pressure on Russia and delayed missile deliveries that threaten Ukrainian lives. He also blasted Donald Trump's public embrace of Vladimir Putin, likening it to befriending Adolf Hitler. Meanwhile, peace talks remain deadlocked as negotiators prepare to resume discussions in December.

stories.headline: NFL Week 12 Outlook: Steelers Face Playoff Jeopardy Without Aaron Rodgers
stories.summary: CBS Sports previews Week 12 NFL matchups, highlighting the Pittsburgh Steelers' precarious position in the playoff race as they navigate games without Aaron Rodgers. Analysts offer predictions and insights on key Thanksgiving week matchups.

stories.headline: Bills and Chiefs Clash in Latest Chapter of Allen-Mahomes Rivalry
stories.summary: CBS Sports breaks down the latest high-stakes matchup between Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes. The Thanksgiving football preview examines odds, viewing details, and keys to victory for the marquee game.

stories.headline: sqlite3_rsync Enables Direct Remote Backups for SQLite
stories.summary: The sqlite3_rsync tool allows users to pull snapshot copies of a SQLite database over an SSH connection without requiring local disk space to build a full duplicate. By exchanging cryptographic page hashes, it synchronizes data efficiently across a network. This utility avoids the local storage limitations typically encountered with traditional backup APIs or VACUUM INTO commands.

stories.headline: Understanding Jumper's Knee: Causes, Symptoms, and Rehab for Volleyball Players
stories.summary: Patellar tendinopathy, commonly known as jumper's knee, is an overuse injury driven heavily by high jump volumes and match loads in volleyball. Research indicates that a progressive strength training program is far more effective for recovery than rest alone.

stories.headline: ‘Help! My Bible Reading Feels Dead’ – A Call to Revitalize Personal Study
stories.summary: The Gospel Coalition piece addresses the common sense of stagnation in daily Scripture reading and offers practical steps to restore engagement and spiritual vitality.

stories.headline: The Hidden Challenges of Discussing AI Anxiety
stories.summary: An essay explores the underlying reasons why people find it difficult to openly address and debate their fears surrounding the rapid advancement and societal impact of artificial intelligence.

stories.headline: Myanmar Rejects Portions of Historic ICJ Genocide Ruling
stories.summary: Military leader Min Aung Hlaing announced that Myanmar will refuse to comply with what it deems inappropriate parts of the International Court of Justice's landmark genocide ruling. The ICJ previously found Myanmar in violation of the 1948 Genocide Convention for its 2017 military crackdown against the Rohingya minority. While the court ordered reparations and investigations, it lacks enforcement power and relies on international political pressure.

stories.headline: FCC Approves SpaceX Plan for 1 Million Orbital Satellites Amid Scientific Skepticism
stories.summary: The Trump administration has authorized SpaceX to deploy one million satellites to form 'Starmind,' a constellation of space-based data centers intended to process massive AI workloads. While the FCC lauds the historic initiative, the announcement has sparked alarm and skepticism among scientists.

stories.headline: Pete Prisco's Week 12 NFL Predictions
stories.summary: CBS Sports expert Pete Prisco shares his predictions and analysis for the Week 12 NFL slate. Key matchups featured include the Cleveland Browns facing the Raiders and the Pittsburgh Steelers working to overcome internal issues against the Broncos.

stories.headline: NFL Week 12 Expert Picks and Matchup Analysis
stories.summary: CBS Sports analysts face off with competing predictions for crucial Week 12 NFL matchups. The slate highlights high-profile games including Broncos at Steelers and Seahawks at 49ers.

stories.headline: Two Italian Rheinmetall Technicians Killed in Kuwait Strike
stories.summary: Two Italian nationals working as defense technicians for Rheinmetall were killed in Kuwait by falling shrapnel from intercepted drones. Both Italy and Kuwait blamed Iran for the attack, while Tehran denied responsibility and called the incident suspicious. The strike escalates regional tensions following recent deadlocked negotiations and military exchanges.

stories.headline: Pop Stars Pay Tribute to Late Duran Duran Guitarist Andy Taylor
stories.summary: Fellow musicians including Simon Le Bon, Sir Rod Stewart, and Gary Kemp are honoring Andy Taylor following his death at age 65. Duran Duran's members remembered his vital role in giving the band its rock edge, while his wife Tracey called him the rock of their family. Taylor passed away peacefully at home on November 23 after a courageous battle with prostate cancer.

stories.headline: Duran Duran Guitarist Andy Taylor Dies at 65
stories.summary: Andy Taylor, the original guitarist for the 1980s new wave band Duran Duran, has passed away at the age of 65. His family and bandmates confirmed his death, following his public revelation in 2022 that he was battling Stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer. Taylor's distinct guitar work defined massive hits like "Hungry Like the Wolf" and helped shape the band's signature sound.

stories.headline: Eagles vs. Cowboys Thanksgiving Betting Preview and Predictions
stories.summary: CBS Sports provides a comprehensive betting breakdown for the traditional Thanksgiving Day matchup between the Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys. The preview includes opening odds, expert picks, and key lines to watch for the NFC East rivalry.

stories.headline: 1Password Discloses Backend Breach Involving Employee GitHub Account
stories.summary: 1Password revealed that an attacker used a compromised corporate GitHub account to access source code and administrative customer data. The exposed records include names, email addresses, and account metadata, though no customer vault contents were accessed. In response, the company has rotated exposed credentials and strengthened security measures by expanding user recovery codes from six to ten digits.

stories.headline: The New York Times Strict Photojournalism Standards Bar AI Edits
stories.summary: A recent account from a New York Times photo shoot highlights the publication's zero-tolerance policy for digital alterations. Photographers are instructed not to use AI tools like those in updated versions of Photoshop, even to remove minor flaws like a stain on a shirt. The newspaper maintains that images must authentically reflect reality as captured through natural lighting and traditional framing.

stories.headline: Scott Aaronson Compares AI Breakthroughs to Scientific Revolutions
stories.summary: A shared quote from complexity theorist Scott Aaronson likens the recent expansion of mathematical truth unlocked by advanced AI to historical milestones like the invention of the microscope and telescope. He suggests researchers are now exploring an entirely new continent of mathematical complexity that was previously hidden.

stories.headline: datasette-charts 0.3a0 Introduces Custom Chart Annotations
stories.summary: Simon Willison released datasette-charts 0.3a0, adding support for visual chart annotations like lines, shaded areas, and labels. Users can interactively build and tweak these annotations directly within Datasette Lite's UI. The update also integrates with Datasette Agent to let AI assistants automatically generate annotated charts.

stories.headline: Nextcloud Launches Euro-Office Desktop App for Sovereign Productivity
stories.summary: Nextcloud has released its official desktop office app powered by Euro-Office, a sovereign European collaborative suite. Available for Windows, macOS, and Linux, the free and open-source tool supports offline editing and high compatibility with Microsoft Office formats. Users can also connect the application to Nextcloud Hub for real-time team collaboration and cloud file access.

stories.headline: Finding Comfort in Christmas Amid Heavy News
stories.summary: For those fatigued by a relentless and exhausting news cycle, the Christmas season offers a welcoming anchor of enduring hope. The narrative of the holiday provides spiritual relief and a reminder of grace for a weary public.

stories.headline: Reflecting on the Value and History of Evangelical Publishing
stories.summary: An essay from The Gospel Coalition explores the historical and ongoing significance of evangelical publishing within the Christian faith. It highlights prominent theological resources and influential figures shaping contemporary religious literature. The piece underscores how traditional texts and modern commentaries continue to support church communities and spiritual growth.

stories.headline: Isak Finding His Rhythm at Liverpool After Injury-Plagued Start
stories.summary: After enduring a delayed start and a broken leg following his expensive move from Newcastle, striker Alexander Isak is finally delivering for Liverpool. With a recent double against Club Brugge, he has reached 10 goals for the season and joined an elite group of players to score in six consecutive away matches.

stories.headline: Severe Storms Ravage US Coasts Ahead of Thanksgiving
stories.summary: Powerful storms have struck both U.S. coasts at the start of the Thanksgiving holiday weekend, leaving hundreds of thousands without power. States including Virginia, North Carolina, and New Jersey experienced severe winds that tore roofs off houses and submerged streets in floodwater. The extreme weather has also forced the cancellation of hundreds of flights.

stories.headline: German Boat Dealer Linked to Channel Migrant Smuggling Rings
stories.summary: European authorities suspect German boat dealer Marvin Reuter of supplying nearly a third of the small boats used by migrant smugglers in the English Channel during early 2026. Investigative reports reveal equipment from his firm, MaReBoote, was tied to two fatal accidents resulting in four deaths. Reuter is currently contesting extradition to France to face charges including smuggling and involuntary manslaughter.

stories.headline: BBC Confronts German Supplier Suspected of Fueling Channel Smuggling
stories.summary: German boat dealer Marvin Reuter is facing scrutiny as a key supplier for migrant smuggling operations in the English Channel. Files indicate nearly a third of small-boat crossings to the UK in early 2026 utilized vessels or engines from his company, MaReBoote. Reuter declined to answer questions from journalists and is currently fighting extradition to France.

stories.headline: Diesel Tanker Capsizes Off Ibiza Coast, Leaving One Crew Member Dead
stories.summary: A Malta-flagged chemical tanker carrying up to 7,000 tonnes of diesel capsized 25 nautical miles off the coast of Ibiza. While 16 of the 17 crew members were rescued with minor injuries, one hospitalized crew member was later pronounced dead. Spanish authorities and a pollution control vessel were deployed to monitor the partially submerged wreck for potential environmental impacts.

stories.headline: Iranian Women Facing Death Row Desperately Appeal Following Protests
stories.summary: Six women, including 21-year-old twin sisters Romina and Taraneh Rahimi, have been sentenced to death in Iran following anti-government demonstrations. Human rights advocates warn of an unprecedented surge in politically motivated executions targeting female dissidents and protesters.

stories.headline: Severe Storms Disrupt Holiday Travel and NYC Parade
stories.summary: Powerful storms sweeping across the East Coast threaten severe travel delays and coastal flooding during the Thanksgiving holiday. In New York City, winds reaching up to 60 mph forced officials to reschedule the centennial Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday. Meanwhile, legal developments show a judge ruling that the FCC violated ABC's free speech.

stories.headline: Puerto Rico Supreme Court Voids Contract for Power Grid Operator LUMA
stories.summary: The Puerto Rico Supreme Court has ruled in favor of the governor, allowing the territory to terminate its contract with LUMA Energy after five years of managing the troubled power grid. The government now has one year to select and transition to a new operator.

stories.headline: Google Play Requires Developer Trader Declarations by February 2027
stories.summary: Google is requiring all active Play Console developers to declare whether they operate as commercial traders or non-traders under EEA and UK laws by February 1, 2027. Developers who qualify as traders based on profit motives, transaction volume, or business setups must make their status visible to consumers in those regions. Non-traders distributing apps outside commercial contexts can declare accordingly to reflect consumer rights applicability.

stories.headline: Spotlighting Kamil Khan Mumtaz, Pakistan's Overlooked Architectural Master
stories.summary: Kamil Khan Mumtaz has emerged as a celebrated yet internationally invisible architect crafting traditional buildings in Lahore, Pakistan. Born in Calcutta in 1939, Mumtaz studied in London before returning to Pakistan in 1966 to build a career marked by both architectural innovation and political activism. A new portfolio highlights his remarkable traditional designs, which rarely receive attention outside of South Asia.
